title: Newcastle United 2-2 Arsenal: Madueke snatches draw as Raya goes off injured in second-half thriller
subtitle: Arsenal lost David Raya to injury, but Noni Madueke's goal at least ensured the Premier League leaders did not go down to Newcastle United.
paragraphs: Newcastle United's superb second-half fightback was not enough to beat Arsenal, as Noni Madueke's 78th-minute goal sealed a 2-2 draw at St James' Park.
Premier League leaders Arsenal went into Saturday's contest buoyed by Manchester City's latest slip-up, with Enzo Maresca's team failing to beat Fulham earlier on.
But the Gunners could not get a win that would have seen them move eight points clear, ahead of second-place Brighton facing Hull City on Sunday.
Matthias Jaissle might not have got the big win he needed to really kickstart his tenure, but Newcastle looked much more akin to the team that impressed so regularly under Eddie Howe after the break.

Arsenal were utterly dominant before half-time, though. Madueke hit the woodwork, former Newcastle fan favourite Bruno Guimaraes went close, and the Gunners deservedly took the lead when Eberechi Eze finished from Kai Havertz’s throughball in the 33rd minute.
Madueke was denied by Lukas Hornicek and a fantastic Lewis Hall block before half-time, and Newcastle made those reprieves count.
After David Raya received treatment for a knock, Martin Odegaard's mistake four minutes into the second half allowed William Osula to feed Harvey Barnes, who tucked in his 100th career goal.
The comeback was complete 13 minutes later. Hall's corner was met by Dan Burn, and amid a goalmouth scramble, Malick Thiaw nudged home.

Raya then trudged off with an apparent arm injury as Arsenal's frustration was compounded, but Newcastle – who went close to a third when Havertz's defensive header from Hall's corner clip the Gunners' crossbar – could not keep the momentum going.

Arsenal countered at pace, with Odegaard finding Madueke, who skipped onto his left foot and shot through Burn's legs, with Hornicek making a poor attempt at the save as the Gunners ensured a share of the spoils.
Newcastle had just three shots (0 on target), one touch in the opposition's box, and won 46% of their duels in the first half, while facing 11 shots themselves (three on target).
In the second half, they had nine shots (three on target), 14 touches in the opposition’s box, and won 52.5% of their duels, facing just two shots from Arsenal (one on target).
In fact, Newcastle's first-half expected goals tally came out at just 0.08. Yet they finished with 1.78 xG to Arsenal's 1.38.
But Newcastle could not get over the line, as their defensive fragility came back to bite them. Only five teams have shipped more Premier League goals than the Magpies this term.
Arsenal's backline lacked its usual solidity, though, and Mikel Arteta will likely feel plenty of relief at having come away with a point.
This result ended a 21-game run of Premier League games without a draw for the Gunners (W18 D3) since a 2-2 draw with Wolves back in February.
Indeed, this was just the second draw in the last 28 Premier League meetings between Arsenal (22 wins) and Newcastle (four), after a 0-0 at Emirates Stadium in January 2023.

Premier League leaders Arsenal went into Saturday's contest buoyed by Manchester City's latest slip-up, with Enzo Maresca's team failing to beat Fulham earlier on.

But the Gunners could not get a win that would have seen them move eight points clear, ahead of second-place Brighton facing Hull City on Sunday.

Matthias Jaissle might not have got the big win he needed to really kickstart his tenure, but Newcastle looked much more akin to the team that impressed so regularly under Eddie Howe after the break.

Arsenal were utterly dominant before half-time, though. Madueke hit the woodwork, former Newcastle fan favourite Bruno Guimaraes went close, and the Gunners deservedly took the lead when Eberechi Eze finished from Kai Havertz’s throughball in the 33rd minute.

Madueke was denied by Lukas Hornicek and a fantastic Lewis Hall block before half-time, and Newcastle made those reprieves count.

Arsenal countered at pace, with Odegaard finding Madueke, who skipped onto his left foot and shot through Burn's legs, with Hornicek making a poor attempt at the save as the Gunners ensured a share of the spoils.

A game of two halves

Newcastle had just three shots (0 on target), one touch in the opposition's box, and won 46% of their duels in the first half, while facing 11 shots themselves (three on target).

In the second half, they had nine shots (three on target), 14 touches in the opposition’s box, and won 52.5% of their duels, facing just two shots from Arsenal (one on target).

In fact, Newcastle's first-half expected goals tally came out at just 0.08. Yet they finished with 1.78 xG to Arsenal's 1.38.

This result ended a 21-game run of Premier League games without a draw for the Gunners (W18 D3) since a 2-2 draw with Wolves back in February.

Indeed, this was just the second draw in the last 28 Premier League meetings between Arsenal (22 wins) and Newcastle (four), after a 0-0 at Emirates Stadium in January 2023.
